recipes.name: 5-Ingredient Mexican Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 cups shredded Cheddar or Colby Jack cheese

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Spray a 9-inch pie pan with non-stick cooking spray.
In a saucepan, cook refried beans and onions (to soften them) on medium-high heat for about 5 minutes.

Place one tortilla in the bottom of the greased pan. Spread about 1/3 cup of the bean mixture over it. Layer a few tablespoons of salsa over this. Then, place another tortilla over the salsa, and add more of the bean mixture. Follow the beans with a big handful of cheese, spreading evenly. repeat layers, spreading the ingredients evenly over the tortillas. On the top layer, make sure to use lots of salsa and cheese!
Bake until the cheese is melted, approximately 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: 5-Ingredient Mexican Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Small dinner pie made with salsa, tortillas, refried beans, cheese, and onions.

video.description: Watch how you can create a layered baked pie with Mexican-inspired staple ingredients. This vegetarian version of the casserole uses refried beans, onion, tortillas, jarred salsa and shredded cheese.

review.reviewBody: Not being vegetarian, I warmed up some leftover taco-seasoned ground beef in a separate skillet and layered that over the beans in each repetition. Adding this, I ended up doing 2 complete layer repetitions and using fewer tortillas, less salsa and less cheese (used the packaged 4-cheese Mexican blend) than the recipe called for. I cut it just like a pie and topped each piece to be served with a spoonful of sour cream. It looked and smelled very appetizing and my family enjoyed it a lot, especially my 4 year old son. This was very easy, tasty, and it should be great for leftovers. Plus, I had all the ingredients on hand so it was convenient too. Thanks!

This turned out absolutely delicious! I used corn tortillas instead of flour tortillas. I like texture and flavor of corn better. Cooked a pound of ground beef and a pound of ground turkey and used that to replace the 2nd layer of the refried beans. Then, after I removed from oven, I put sour cream as another layer on top. Now, my bake pan is bigger so I can use a 16 oz sour cream to layer it on top. I also cut up green onions and topped it off! Used blue corn chips as a side with salsa. My family loved it! This one is definitely a keeper.

This is a great base for a wonderful meal. I did sauté the onions with a little garlic before adding the beans to the pan with a little bit of salsa added to make it easier to spread. I also browned some ground beef with some salt, pepper, cumin, and chili powder. In 2 oiled cast iron skillets I layered tortilla, beans, beef, corn, salsa, cheese, and repeated once so each skillet had two levels. Baked for about 20 minutes. This came out great. Everyone loved it. Definitely a keeper. Kudos to the simplicity that can spawn a hearty, tasty meal.

made as is the recipe is bland and mushy like other reviews have said. It needs some spice, some seasoning, a little love (seasoning) in your dish goes a long way. there's no love in this dish, it's just plain ingredients. it definitely needs texture. I made this first the other day as the recipe is written with no changes and it was not good. I made it last night using some of the advice of other reviews and added taco seasoned ground beef, chili peppers, and corn. i added garlic to the beans. And you have to cook the onions separate from the beans then mix them in otherwise you get under cooked onions and burned beans. I used sweet onions and caramelized them and heated the refried beans in another pan while they cooked. then mixed them together with the canned chilis, layered like instructed adding the beef on top of the beans. My pan held 2 full layers, and then i sprinkled fresh cilantro and chopped up black olivers on top and covered with a good layer of cheese. Have to say it was really really good with these changes. My son asked to make it again this weekend so he could take some to work and share with a couple friends.

I had to make some modifications but they were well worth it. Here's what you should consider: add 1 can corn and 1 can black beans; mix corn, black beans, salsa, sautéed onions, and refried beans in a large bowl before layering in the casserole dish; finish with a sprinkle of seasoning over all; finally bake until sides are bubbling. Serve with chips and enjoy.

Made this using 1 LB Al Pastor seasoned beef, small can of Rotel, medium yellow onion, can of refried beans, can of Hormel no-bean chili, a cup of salsa and cooked down until nice and thick. Then added it to 5-10 inch tortillas with a mixture of Monterey Jack and Cheddar cheeses. Cooked it in a oven rated skillet until nice and bubbly. Really very tasty! Next time I will assemble and cook on the stove top to crisp up the bottom tortilla before placing in the oven. The extras I added took it to the next level, but there is sooo much you can do to this recipe to take it way beyond next level.
MY only adjustment was adding seasoned ground beef. Turned out excellent.

I used corn tortillas and added spinach. Turned out great. Obviously you could choose to add meat or Not and you can buy lard free beans or Not. You do you. It's still a great concept recipe that you can make your own. Xoxo.

5 ingredient dinner is always a winner in my house. Did not have refried beans so made my own with a can of black beans & a potato masher. I had black bean & corn salsa on hand & pepper jack cheese.I used 4 tortillas: Smothered tort with refried, then salsa, then cheese> next tort Refried, salsa & cheese> next tort refried, salsa & cheese and just covered the top tort with cheese. So easy and delish. Will definitely make again....probably bigger portion in a lasagna pan
We loved it, but I did slightly revise the recipe. I don't usually do that but we love enchilada sauce. I added it between the layers and with the cheese on top. It was even better the second day.

I loved this. I used fat free refried beans, medium salsa and added 1/2 ground turkey with 1/2 lb very lean ground beef. I used 1/2 t hot and spicy taco seasoning and some reg taco seasoning, to your liking. It was fantastic.

Sauteed onions and garlic and red pepper, then added shredded chicken, cumin, and taco sauce. Finally added the refried beans. Top with lettuce and tomato and sour cream. Could do black beans instead of chicken.
Easy weeknight dinner. I added shredded chicken and black beans. Could have used some taco seasoning. Served with sour cream and street corn. Hit the spot!
My one son thought it was great as is, other thought it would be better if I added chicken to it
I loved making this recipe. Easy to make and delicious.
Easy and quick. I used corn tortillas. The dish was firm and sliced easily. This will be a new base dish for my Mexican culinary adventures!
I added a few jalapeños pieces yummy it was delicious I love it and my husband loves it too
Quick and easy. Tastes great.
Love this simple recipe
Very easy. Added ground beef to the refried beans.
